items.question: What can result from loading the R22 outside its weight and balance limits?
options: Insufficient control travel for safe operation
An overweight landing gear failure only
items.explanation: The helicopter must be flown only within the weight and balance limits specified in Section 2. Loadings outside these limits can result in insufficient control travel for safe operation.

items.question: How is the R22 center of gravity adjusted when needed?
options: By adding removable ballast to an under-seat baggage compartment, then recalculating weight and balance and checking compartment limits
items.explanation: The CG may be adjusted by adding removable ballast (any appropriate item of mass) to an under-seat baggage compartment. Recalculate weight and balance after adding ballast, and verify the ballast meets the baggage compartment limits in Section 2.

items.question: Which way does the R22 CG move as fuel is burned during flight, and what can this limit?
options: Aft; it can limit aft loading
Forward; payload may be limited by forward CG as fuel is burned
items.explanation: A caution: fuel burn causes CG to move forward during flight. Always determine safe loading with empty fuel as well as with takeoff fuel; payload may be limited by forward CG as fuel is burned.

items.question: Which two fuel conditions must both be checked to be within CG limits?
options: Takeoff fuel and empty (zero usable) fuel
Main tank only and aux tank only
items.explanation: Calculated weight and balance must be compared with the Section 2 CG limits; both the takeoff-fuel and empty-fuel conditions must be within limits.

items.question: What fuel weight is used in the R22 sample loading calculation?
items.explanation: The sample loading calculation uses usable main and aux fuel at 6 lb/gal.
references: R22 POH Sec 6: LOADING INSTRUCTIONS – Sample Loading Calculation (p.6-6)

items.question: What is the longitudinal arm of the pilot and baggage under the right seat in the Common Item Weight & CG table?
items.explanation: The Common Item Weight & CG table gives a longitudinal arm of 78.0 in for pilot and baggage under the right seat and for passenger and baggage under the left seat (use 79.0 in for aircraft prior to S/N 0256 with early-style seats).
references: R22 POH Sec 6: LOADING INSTRUCTIONS – Common Item Weight & CG (p.6-4)

items.question: What is the lateral reference datum for R22 weight and balance?
options: The aircraft centerline, with items to the right positive and items to the left negative
The main rotor mast, right negative
items.explanation: The lateral reference datum is the aircraft centerline; items to the right are positive and items to the left are negative. Lateral CG usually falls well within limits for conventional loadings.

items.question: How is the loaded helicopter CG (arm) determined?
options: By dividing the total moment by the total weight
By subtracting the empty weight arm from the datum
items.explanation: The CG location (arm) for the loaded helicopter is determined by dividing the total moment by the total weight.
references: R22 POH Sec 6: LOADING INSTRUCTIONS – Sample Loading Calculation (p.6-6)

items.question: With both doors installed, what minimum solo pilot plus baggage weight ensures the R22 CG stays within limits?
options: 135 lb (61 kg) — 130 lb without the auxiliary fuel tank
items.explanation: A note: with both doors installed, a solo pilot plus baggage weight of 135 lb (61 kg) or greater ensures CG within limits (130 lb without the auxiliary fuel tank). For lower weight, compute weight and balance; removable ballast may be required to obtain CG at or forward of the aft limit.
references: R22 POH Sec 6: WEIGHT AND BALANCE RECORD note (p.6-2); Sec 2 CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITS (p.2-3)

items.question: What is 'Basic Empty Weight' in the R22 POH definitions?
options: Standard empty weight plus the weight of installed optional equipment
Maximum gross weight minus useful load
items.explanation: Basic Empty Weight is standard empty weight plus the weight of installed optional equipment. Standard Empty Weight is the weight of the standard helicopter including unusable fuel, full operating fluids and full engine oil.
references: R22 POH Sec 1: WEIGHT AND BALANCE DEFINITIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: What is 'Useful Load' defined as?
options: The difference between maximum gross weight and basic empty weight
items.explanation: Useful Load is the difference between maximum gross weight and basic empty weight. Payload is the weight of occupants, cargo and baggage.
references: R22 POH Sec 1: WEIGHT AND BALANCE DEFINITIONS (p.1-7)

items.question: When must an entry be made in the R22 Weight and Balance Record?
options: Each time an item of equipment is removed or installed, with the new empty CG determined
items.explanation: Each time an item of equipment is removed or installed, an entry must be made in the Weight and Balance Record and the new empty CG determined. The original factory weight and balance provides the first entry.
references: R22 POH Sec 6: WEIGHT AND BALANCE RECORD (p.6-2)
